title: Two-Step Inequalities
seo_title: Grade 7 Two-Step Inequalities Worksheets: Solve, Graph and Word Problems
standard_text: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 two-step inequalities worksheets: inequality symbols and graphs, solving px + q > r, reversing the sign when dividing by a negative, graphing solutions, and word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Solve like an equation, but flip the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
key_sub: −3x + 1 ≤ 7 → −3x ≤ 6 → x ≥ −2. Open circle for < and >, closed circle for ≤ and ≥.
body_html:
Solve like an equation

Undo the steps in reverse order, just like a two-step equation. There is one new rule: when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign.

InequalityStep 1ResultStep 2Solution
2x + 3 > 11subtract 32x > 8divide by 2x > 4
−3x + 1 ≤ 7subtract 1−3x ≤ 6divide by −3, flipx ≥ −2

Graph the solutions

Use an open circle for > and < (the number is not included) and a closed circle for ≥ and ≤ (it is included). Draw the arrow toward the numbers that work.

Example

You have $40. Shirts cost $12 each and shipping is $4. How many shirts can you buy?

Write: 12s + 4 ≤ 40.

Subtract 4: 12s ≤ 36.

Divide by 12: s ≤ 3.

Answer: at most 3 shirts

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to flip: −2x > 8 gives x < −4, not x > −4.
  • Flipping when you should not: 2x > −8 gives x > −4. The sign flips only when you divide by a negative.
  • Using the wrong circle: ≥ and ≤ get a closed circle.

faq.q: How do you solve a two-step inequality?
faq.a: Undo the adding or subtracting, then undo the multiplying or dividing. For 2x + 3 > 11: 2x > 8, so x > 4.

faq.q: When do you flip the inequality sign?
faq.a: Only when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number. −2x > 8 becomes x < −4.
Use an open circle for < and > because the number is not a solution. Use a closed circle for ≤ and ≥ because it is.

faq.q: How do I write an inequality from words?
faq.a: At most means ≤, at least means ≥, more than means >, and less than means <. $3 plus $2 per mile for at most $25 is 2m + 3 ≤ 25.

items.q: What does x > 3 mean?
c: x is less than or equal to 3
x is greater than or equal to 3
items.e: x > 3 means greater than. The symbol > includes the number itself only if it has a line under it.

items.q: What does x ≤ −2 mean?
c: x is greater than or equal to −2
x is less than or equal to −2
items.e: x ≤ −2 means less than or equal to. The symbol ≤ includes the number itself only if it has a line under it.

items.q: What does x < 7 mean?
c: x is greater than or equal to 7
x is less than or equal to 7
items.e: x < 7 means less than. The symbol < includes the number itself only if it has a line under it.

items.q: What does x ≥ 0 mean?
c: x is greater than or equal to 0
x is less than or equal to 0
items.e: x ≥ 0 means greater than or equal to. The symbol ≥ includes the number itself only if it has a line under it.

items.q: Is x = 5 a solution of 2x + 3 > 11?
items.e: Put 5 in for x: 2(5) + 3 = 13. Is 13 > 11? Yes.

items.q: Is x = 4 a solution of 3x − 4 ≤ 8?
items.e: Put 4 in for x: 3(4) − 4 = 8. Is 8 ≤ 8? Yes.

items.q: Is x = 4 a solution of 2x + 1 < 9?
items.e: Put 4 in for x: 2(4) + 1 = 9. Is 9 < 9? No.

items.q: Is x = 3 a solution of −2x + 5 ≥ 1?
Is x = 3 a solution of 4x + 1 > 13?
items.e: Put 3 in for x: 4(3) + 1 = 13. Is 13 > 13? No.

items.q: Is x = 4 a solution of −3x + 2 < -7?
Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at 2 and open (the number is not included). The arrow points right, so the numbers are greater than 2: x > 2.

items.q: Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at −1 and filled in (the number is included). The arrow points left, so the numbers are less than or equal to −1: x ≤ −1.

items.q: Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at 4 and filled in (the number is included). The arrow points right, so the numbers are greater than or equal to 4: x ≥ 4.

items.q: Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at 0 and open (the number is not included). The arrow points left, so the numbers are less than 0: x < 0.

items.q: Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at −3 and open (the number is not included). The arrow points right, so the numbers are greater than −3: x > −3.

items.q: Which inequality does the graph show?
items.e: The circle is at 6 and filled in (the number is included). The arrow points left, so the numbers are less than or equal to 6: x ≤ 6.

items.q: Which number is a solution of x < −2?
items.e: −5 is to the left of −2 on the number line, so −5 < −2. −2 itself is not a solution because the sign is <, not ≤.

items.q: Which number is a solution of x ≥ 6?
items.e: ≥ includes 6 itself, so 6 is a solution.

items.q: How many solutions does x > 4 have?
items.e: Every number greater than 4 works, like 4.1, 5 and 100. An inequality usually has infinitely many solutions.

items.q: Which symbol means at least?
items.e: At least 10 means 10 or more: ≥ 10. At most means ≤.

items.q: Solve 2x + 3 > 11.
items.e: Subtract 3 from both sides: 2x > 8. Divide both sides by 2: x > 4.

items.q: Solve 3x − 4 < 14.
items.e: Add 4 to both sides: 3x < 18. Divide both sides by 3: x < 6.
Subtract 5 from both sides: 4x ≥ 20. Divide both sides by 4: x ≥ 5.
Add 2 to both sides: 5x ≤ 20. Divide both sides by 5: x ≤ 4.

items.q: Solve 2x + 7 > 3.
items.e: Subtract 7 from both sides: 2x > −4. Divide both sides by 2: x > −2.

items.q: Solve 6x + 1 < 31.
items.e: Subtract 1 from both sides: 6x < 30. Divide both sides by 6: x < 5.
Subtract 8 from both sides: 3x ≥ −9. Divide both sides by 3: x ≥ −3.
Add 3 to both sides: 7x ≤ 28. Divide both sides by 7: x ≤ 4.

items.q: Solve 4x − 10 > 6.
items.e: Add 10 to both sides: 4x > 16. Divide both sides by 4: x > 4.
Subtract 6 from both sides: 8x < −16. Divide both sides by 8: x < −2.
Subtract 9 from both sides: 2x ≥ 12. Divide both sides by 2: x ≥ 6.
Add 5 to both sides: 10x ≤ 50. Divide both sides by 10: x ≤ 5.

items.e: Subtract 12 from both sides: 5x > −10. Divide both sides by 5: x > −2.
Add 6 to both sides: 3x < −9. Divide both sides by 3: x < −3.
Subtract 4 from both sides: 9x ≥ 36. Divide both sides by 9: x ≥ 4.

Subtract 4 from both sides: 2.5x ≥ 15. Divide both sides by 2.5: x ≥ 6.
Subtract 3 from both sides: −2x > 8. Divide both sides by −2: x < −4. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x > −4: the sign must flip.
Subtract 1 from both sides: −3x < −9. Divide both sides by −3: x > 3. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x < 3: the sign must flip.
Add 5 to both sides: −4x ≥ 20. Divide both sides by −4: x ≤ −5. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x ≥ −5: the sign must flip.
Subtract 6 from both sides: −x ≤ −4. Divide both sides by −1: x ≥ 4. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x ≤ 4: the sign must flip.
Subtract 2 from both sides: −5x < 20. Divide both sides by −5: x > −4. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x < −4: the sign must flip.
Add 7 to both sides: −2x > 6. Divide both sides by −2: x < −3. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x > −3: the sign must flip.

items.q: Solve −x − 2 > 5.
items.e: Add 2 to both sides: −x > 7. Divide both sides by −1: x < −7. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x > −7: the sign must flip.
Subtract 10 from both sides: −4x < 20. Divide both sides by −4: x > −5. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x < −5: the sign must flip.
Subtract 3 from both sides: −7x ≤ −21. Divide both sides by −7: x ≥ 3. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x ≤ 3: the sign must flip.
Subtract 1 from both sides: −2x ≥ 0. Divide both sides by −2: x ≤ 0. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x ≥ 0: the sign must flip.
Add 5 to both sides: −5x > 25. Divide both sides by −5: x < −5. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x > −5: the sign must flip.
Subtract 6 from both sides: −8x < −8. Divide both sides by −8: x > 1. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign. Not x < 1: the sign must flip.

items.q: When do you reverse the inequality sign?
c: Whenever there is a negative number in the inequality
When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number
When you add or subtract a negative number
items.e: Only multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the sign. Example: −2x > 6 gives x < −3. Adding or subtracting never reverses it.

items.q: Solve −x < 4.
items.e: −x < 4 means −1 × x < 4. Divide by −1 and flip: x > −4.

items.q: Ana solved −3x + 2 ≥ 14 and got x ≥ −4. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not reverse the sign when dividing by −3.
items.e: −3x ≥ 12. Dividing by −3 flips the sign: x ≤ −4.

items.q: Which inequality has the same solutions as −4x > 8?
items.e: Divide by −4 and flip the sign: x < −2.
Subtract 5: −2x ≤ 6. Divide by −2 and flip: x ≥ −3.

items.q: Solve 12 − 3x > 0.
items.e: Subtract 12: −3x > −12. Divide by −3 and flip: x < 4.

items.q: Leo has $40 and wants to buy shirts that cost $12 each. Which inequality shows how many shirts (s) he can buy?
items.e: The total cost 12s must be at most $40: 12s ≤ 40.

items.q: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. You can spend at most $25. How many miles can you ride?
Lily has $35 in savings and saves $15 a week. How many weeks until she has more than $200?
A gym charges $50 to join and $20 a month. Your budget is $230. For how many months can you go?
You need at least 90 points. You have 54 points, and each quiz is worth 6 points. How many quizzes must you pass?
An elevator can hold at most 1,200 pounds. A worker weighs 180 pounds and brings boxes of 60 pounds each. How many boxes can go?
A phone has 80% battery and loses 4% each hour. When will it be below 20%?
items.e: 80 − 4h < 20, so −4h < −60. Divide by −4 and flip: h > 15.

items.q: A school club has $120. It spends $15 on each event and must keep more than $30. How many events can it hold?
items.e: 120 − 15e > 30, so −15e > −90. Divide by −15 and flip: e < 6. So at most 5 events.

items.q: Which inequality says: 3 more than twice a number is at least 15?
items.e: Twice a number is 2n, 3 more is 2n + 3, and at least means ≥.

items.q: Which inequality says: 5 less than 4 times a number is less than 23?
items.e: 4 times a number is 4n; 5 less is 4n − 5.

items.q: A pool is being drained. It has 900 gallons and loses 50 gallons a minute. When will it have less than 300 gallons?
Maya earns $9 an hour and wants to earn at least $150 for a bike. She already has $42. How many hours must she work?
A rectangle has length 10 cm and width w cm. Its perimeter must be less than 36 cm. What are the possible widths?
Movie tickets cost $11 and popcorn is $7. A group buys one popcorn and spends no more than $73. How many tickets can it buy?
The temperature is 5°F and falls 3°F each hour. When will it be below −10°F?
items.e: 5 − 3h < −10, so −3h < −15 and h > 5 (flip the sign).

items.q: A box can hold at most 25 kg. The empty box weighs 1.5 kg. Each book weighs 0.5 kg. How many books fit?
You must score more than 80 on average over two tests. You got 74 on the first. What must you get on the second?
Which value of x is NOT a solution of 3x − 2 > 7?
items.e: 3x − 2 > 7 gives x > 3. 3 itself is not greater than 3.

items.q: A plumber charges $60 plus $45 an hour. The job must cost at most $285. What is the longest the job can take?
items.e: 45h + 60 ≤ 285, so 45h ≤ 225 and h ≤ 5. The longest is 5 hours.

items.q: A car rental is $30 a day plus $0.20 a mile. For one day, you want to spend under $60. How far can you drive?
